key_insight: Intensity normalisation can improve MRI segmentation robustness across sites, but it helps less than the broader problem of domain shift.
clinical_relevance: For knee MRI AI tools, choosing a good normalisation method may slightly improve external performance, but cross-scanner generalisability still needs additional solutions.
method: Compared seven intensity normalisation methods for 3D U-Net meniscus segmentation.
Trained on the IWOAI 2019 dataset and tested on both internal and external SKM-TEA data.
Benchmarked standard scaling, histogram-based, CLAHE, and GMM-based approaches.
evidence_signal: Internal performance was similar across methods, but external testing showed significant differences, with Z-score, Nyúl histogram matching, and CLAHE performing more robustly.
watch_item: Normalisation alone did not overcome the large performance drop between datasets, so real-world deployment still depends on handling domain shift.
paper_title: A Systematic Benchmark of Intensity Normalisation Methods for 3D Knee MRI Segmentation and Cross-Domain Generalisability
